prize_parts.citation: for credibly identified evidence on how import competition reshapes local labour markets, employment and earnings

statement.case_for: I keep B044 as a single-part, three-name configuration. The change from round 1 is the citation, not the names or the part. After the exchange I anchor the citation on the trade-shock evidence and local labour-market adjustment, and I no longer write the broader technology-and-tasks claim into it. The reason is attribution. Autor, Dorn and Hanson jointly authored the central China-shock papers, so the three-name part matches the credit without an arbitrary cut. The task-based strand has a lineage that runs through people outside the credited set or already recognised (Katz, Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu), so a citation resting on it would claim more than these three names did. The scientific case is the one I set out in round 1. The design is transparent and has been replicated across countries. It changed how the profession and policymakers think about the cost of adjustment and the distribution of trade gains. A decade of scrutiny has refined magnitudes without overturning the finding that local costs are large and persistent. On the common criteria, I put direct, credible identification of a first-order question first, and attribution clarity second. On clarity of attribution and age, B040 is stronger than B044, and I say so. I still weigh direct evidence of an economic effect above a mechanism whose quantitative validation is indirect. That is a judgement about weighting, not a claim that B040 is weak.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still that this is a research design and a body of empirical findings, not a single conceptual breakthrough. Narrowing the citation to the trade shock sharpens attribution but also makes the achievement look more like empirical application. The identification rests on shift-share instruments with known inference problems. The size and persistence of the effects, and the split between trade and automation, are still contested. The core papers date from about 2013, which is younger than B040 (1997) or B036 (2003). The Committee may also read the recent labour-related recognitions (labour-market work in 2023 and the natural-experiment tradition recognised in 2021, from my general knowledge and not verified here) and the 2024 institutions prize as reducing the marginal case. B040 has the cleanest two-person attribution on the shortlist, and a committee that puts conceptual generality and age first could reasonably choose it.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B040 first and lists B044 as his first alternative with Autor and Hanson only. He says the task-based and trade-shock strands are separable, and that his reservation about B044 weakens considerably if the Committee decides the trade-shock evidence is the achievement.
responses.response: I have moved to the condition he sets. The citation now rests on the trade-shock evidence alone, and the task framework is not claimed. On Dorn I do not agree with a pair. Dorn co-authored the central China-shock papers, and Autor-Hanson would split a three-author design that is unusually cleanly attributable. This is the main attribution cost of the two-name version, and I would not accept it. On his point that the exclusion of Gertler and Gilchrist should rest on the mechanism's independent origin, not on prior recognition, I agree, and I find it persuasive. It is the same principle I apply to Katz: the exclusion rests on a separate strand with its own lineage, not on whether he has been recognised.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B040 first and B044 second. He says that if the Committee prefers B044 he would want it limited to the trade-shock and local-labour-market contribution, with a citation that does not imply the whole technology-and-inequality literature. He sees the instability of the B044 name sets as a real cost.
responses.response: I accept his condition and have redrafted accordingly. The citation is now limited to import competition, local labour markets, employment and earnings. On the instability of the name sets, I think most of it has now been resolved. All four B044 supporters name Autor, Dorn and Hanson, per the chair summary, and my own earlier Katz variant was the outlier, which I withdrew in round 1. I do not claim this makes B044 as clean as B040, where every proposal names the same pair. I do claim the remaining gap is smaller than it looked in the openings.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B040 first. He treats B044 as an alternative because the task-based and trade-shock strands may be separate contributions, because credit is split, and because I left out Dorn in my original Katz version. He also says my argument that B044 has a longer track record than the trade-shock papers alone deserved weight.
responses.response: His split-contribution concern is the reason I narrowed the citation. With the claim limited to the trade-shock papers, the question of whether tasks and trade form one prize-sized achievement no longer has to be answered, and Dorn is included. I still disagree with him on weight. He and I agree that B040's empirical validation is more indirect than its influence on models. I count that as a real difference between the two candidates, whereas he treats it as a caveat that does not change the ranking. I do not dismiss his view that a mechanism with a clean origin is more valuable than a design with debated magnitudes, and my position is a judgement about weighting.

responses.point: Krusell moved from B002 first to B044 first with Autor, Dorn and Hanson, and anchors the citation on trade-shock evidence, not the task framework. He gives maturity as the reason B002 is now an alternative, and he names shift-share inference as the main scientific reservation.
responses.response: We now agree on names and on the citation anchor. I agree that B002 is not yet equal to B044 on maturity, and my reasons are the ones in my round-1 reply: the key results date from 2014 onward and long-run validation of place effects is still emerging. I keep it as an alternative because its measurement and identification standards are compelling and I would want to revisit it as the long-run evidence accumulates. On shift-share inference, I agree that the relevant test is whether the qualitative finding survives the methodological debate. The debate has concerned magnitudes and persistence, and I think the finding has survived. I would still want the citation to avoid any statement about effect size.

responses.point: Dreber-Almenberg ranks B040 first. She argues the citation should rest on the mechanism and its influence on how crises are modelled, not on empirical confirmation of magnitudes, and she says the Committee should state openly that excluding Gertler and Gilchrist favours theory over tested evidence.
responses.response: I take her metascience concern about quantitative validation seriously, and it is the reason I weight direct identification. Her proposed B040 citation, which claims only the mechanism, is honest and does answer my objection to a degree. It does not remove the gap, because a prize for a mechanism still leaves the question of whether the effect is large unanswered. Her point about openly stating what a configuration leaves out applies to B044 as well. If B044 advances, the Committee should say that it credits the trade-shock evidence and not the full task-based and skill-bias literature.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee will judge a research design and a body of empirical findings to carry enough conceptual weight against a mechanism with a clean two-person origin such as B040.
How persistent and how large the China-shock effects are under alternative inference for shift-share designs, and how much of the adjustment is trade rather than automation.
Whether the narrower trade-shock citation leaves out too much of what makes B044 important, since the technology and task strand is then recognised only as context.
Whether recent labour-related and institutions prizes reduce the marginal case or the timing for B044. This rests on my general knowledge and I have not verified it.
How much the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises should reduce the marginal case for B040, which I cannot judge beyond what colleagues have said.
I rely on general knowledge and the supplied materials, not independent verification of citation, replication or impact figures.
statement.conflict_note: No co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson or any other credited name on the shortlist is apparent from my supplied profile. My frequent co-authors are Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner and Bindler, and none is credited. My research on quasi-experimental designs with administrative and archival data is in the same empirical labour tradition as B044, and that field proximity could bias my weighting toward direct identification. I have tried to apply the common criteria. I sit on the Board of Editors of the American Economic Review, which I note as an institutional fact with no tie to any candidate. I also presented the 2023 prize at the announcement, and I do not treat that as evidence of my preferences here. These are disclosed, not adjudicated.
